consumer: The frontend inventory panel renderer asking 'what carried-items entries should I DISPLAY, top-level, as the GUI inventory list shows them?'
scope: The formatted/filtered/stacked inventory-panel view the GUI presents (identical items collapsed into stacked lines with counts, categorized, sorted, and subject to the active inventory filter) — not a flat enumeration of every raw item object.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — flat-iterates ctx.u.wielded_items(), ctx.u.worn, and ctx.u.inv_const_slice() and emits each raw item's type_id/name/symbol/charges, exposing raw simulation-state enumeration rather than the engine's display-formatted inventory view.
divergence: Player carries 5 identical bandages plus a partial and a full magazine: the GUI inventory panel collapses the bandages into one stacked '5x' display line (and applies categorization/sort/active filter), whereas the proposed surface emits five separate flat entries (or splits by charges-stack), so carried_items[] diverges from what the inventory panel would actually show.
